definitions.gloss: feeling of discomfort; unpleasant feeling; displeasure
definitions.explanation: An unpleasant or uncomfortable sensation, whether physical (nausea, irritation) or emotional (annoyance, displeasure). Composed of 不快 (unpleasant) + 感 (feeling).

examples.japanese: {胃|い}に{不快感|ふかいかん}がある。
examples.english: I feel discomfort in my stomach.

examples.japanese: あの{態度|たいど}に{不快感|ふかいかん}を{覚|おぼ}えた{人|ひと}も{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Many people felt displeasure at that attitude.

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}の{副作用|ふくさよう}で{喉|のど}に{不快感|ふかいかん}を{感|かん}じることがある。
examples.english: You may feel discomfort in your throat as a side effect of the medication.

notes:
USAGE:
{不快感|ふかいかん} can describe both physical discomfort (medical contexts) and emotional displeasure (social contexts). It is commonly used in formal or written language.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不快感|ふかいかん}を{覚|おぼ}える (feel discomfort)
- {不快感|ふかいかん}を{感|かん}じる (sense discomfort)
- {不快感|ふかいかん}を{与|あた}える (cause discomfort to others)
- {不快感|ふかいかん}を{示|しめ}す (show displeasure)
- {軽|かる}い{不快感|ふかいかん} (mild discomfort)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{嫌悪感|けんおかん} is stronger — it means "revulsion" or "disgust" rather than mere discomfort. {違和感|いわかん} means a sense that something is off or doesn't feel right, which is more cognitive than physical.
